notes:
Account summary
- Mid-market SaaS building enterprise search / knowledge assistant. Evaluating Redwood as inference layer for doc-search RAG.
- Strong emphasis on operational readiness: they do NOT want to assemble their own stack of retries/timeouts/OTel instrumentation.

What they’re building
- Primary: doc-search experience with citations (internal KB + customer docs). Likely chat UI but core workload is retrieval + answer generation.
- Secondary: support-agent workflows (summarize ticket history + suggest response); wants the same retrieval layer.

Key requirements / asks (from calls)
- “We need something our platform team can ship and own.” Production-minded template is a gating item.
- RAG template must include:
  - ingestion + chunking defaults (they have PDFs/HTML/Markdown)
  - embeddings + retrieval interface they can swap (local dev vs hosted vector DB)
  - answer generation with citations and failure modes handled (empty retrieval, partial retrieval, low-confidence)
  - eval hooks: golden prompt set / regression checks for template upgrades
- Observability:
  - OpenTelemetry traces with meaningful spans (retrieval, rerank if any, generation, tool calls)
  - Metrics they can alert on: p95 latency, tokens (in/out), retrieval hit rate / empty-retrieval rate, tool error rate, 4xx/5xx by category, retry counts
  - Correlation IDs (request-id) present in logs and traces; needs to work across their API gateway
- Resilience / safe defaults:
  - streaming robustness: handle disconnects and retries gracefully
  - sane timeouts/backoff; guardrails for max_tokens / max_iterations
  - log redaction guidance; avoid leaking PII from docs or prompts

Technical notes
- Current stack: Node services + some Python for ML utilities. Preference for TypeScript template first, but OK with Python if docs are strong.
- Wants vendor lock-in minimal: provider abstraction is a plus (they mentioned "we might A/B against Bedrock or our existing provider").
- No hard requirement for VPC today, but they have larger customers asking about private networking; wants a path to Dedicated or Private later.

Success criteria (POC)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end < 2.5s for typical queries on ~8k token context; streaming perceived latency matters.
- Cost: needs clear levers (batching/caching, model choice, token caps). Asked for guidance from Redwood Optimize.
- Quality: basic eval set agreed (20–50 queries) with citations correctness and "no-answer" behavior.
- Operability: dashboards working day 1; error taxonomy aligns with their on-call runbooks.

Risks / objections
- Concern about template telemetry headers being blocked by some corporate proxies (asked if opt-in / configurable).
- Security review: wants explicit statement of what’s logged by default and how to disable/adjust.

Internal ownership / follow-ups
- Monica Patel looped for template + SDK alignment and OTel conventions.
- Next meeting: POC kickoff + define which Redwood-verified model(s) are supported in the template and pinning/fallback approach.
